note: Works properly in the terminal, and updates without the CLI on PATH
detail: Settings in the terminal: cards show their text, the header wraps in a narrow window, short choices are one-press buttons
The terminal bar has Auto on/off, and the effort word flashes on a change like on desktop
Update finds Claude Code in ~/.local/bin when the app cannot see it; with no CLI it says what to install and copies the command
Typing an effort level by name (low, high, max) skips the judge; subagents follow the turn's effort

note: Alerts that stay closed, cheaper handoffs
detail: Close the running-low alert and it stays closed until your limit resets, in new chats too. It comes back once at 95%.
Switch the context, running-low and cold-cache alerts on or off in Settings, under Handoff & alerts.
A quick handoff on a cold cache is now written by Haiku from the chat, instead of rereading the whole chat at full price.
The compact alert waits until 70% of the context by default.
No more warning card under replies: the band above the prompt says it.
New, off by default: Helpers. The judge picks the effort for each subagent too, never below medium.
Compact with moved to the Model card, and cheaper models are marked experimental.
Settings fixes: buttons and cards take clicks edge to edge, Helpers has its own row.

note: Model switching off by default, 21% cheaper than Opus medium
detail: Model switching is off by default. effortless sets the effort and leaves your model alone, because switching models mid-chat costs more than it saves: every model keeps its own cache. You can turn it back on in Settings → Model.
Measured on 96 real coding tasks: 21% cheaper than Opus at medium, 29% cheaper than high and 42% cheaper than xhigh. Every answer was still correct.
Light mode: a new Appearance setting (match Claude Code, dark or light) covers every panel and band.
Fixed: with Auto off, a stale effort was still sent. Now the effort you pick in the app is the one that goes out, and the bar says when your own pick turns Auto off.
/effortless debug shows the model and effort each request ran on.

note: Model card, cherry blossom theme, quality benchmark
detail: New Model card in Settings: keep every prompt on your chat's model, or allow a cheaper one for simple prompts.
New Cherry blossom theme: violets turn pink and the sparkles become falling petals.
The judge benchmark and the answer-quality benchmark are in the repo (bench/RESULTS.md).

note: Haiku compaction keeps your latest work
detail: Haiku compaction keeps your latest messages almost whole, so the most recent work is not summarised away.
The README says where your keys are kept: pasted keys in a plain file, `/plugin configure` in secure storage.

note: The bar shows the model too
detail: The bar shows the model next to the effort, for example High · Opus.
The site and README lead with the model and the effort.
